name: Primary Land Use Tax Lot Output (PLUTO)
publisher: NYC Department of City Planning / NYC Open Data
questions: Which zoning district is reported for this tax lot?
What are the lot area, built FAR and reported residential FAR?
Find a property by address or BBL.
outline: One row per tax lot in the published PLUTO release.
Address and borough identify candidates; BBL links to the selected parcel.
zonedist1 through zonedist4, overlays and special districts describe reported zoning.
lotarea, bldgarea, builtfar, residfar, commfar and facilfar are parcel attributes; version identifies the source release.
instructions: Prefer acres_find_property, which already records retrieved rows as cited evidence.
Resolve ambiguous addresses before selecting a parcel. Preserve BBL for follow-up queries.
Read the release version returned by the API. Cross-check legal conclusions against operative zoning text, maps and applicable approvals.
prerequisites: BBL or address, with borough if ambiguous.
restrictions: Public anonymous small API reads worked at verification. Respect provider throttling; no bulk mirror is required.
limitations: Live API means current published release, not necessarily today's legal status.
Reported FAR does not prove buildable or transferable rights; tax lots and zoning lots are not interchangeable.
verification: 2026-10-11: catalog HTTP 200, name and bbl/address/zonedist1/version fields checked.
2026-10-11: bounded JSON query HTTP 200 returned a parcel with release version 26v2.

name: Mandatory Inclusionary Housing areas
publisher: NYC Department of City Planning / NYC Open Data
questions: Is this site inside a Mandatory Inclusionary Housing area?
Which MIH options apply to this rezoning area?
Does the Universal Affordability Preference or MIH govern this lot?
outline: One multipolygon per adopted MIH area, as mapped in ZR Appendix F.
project_nam, zr_ulurpno and date_adopte identify the rezoning; boro and cd give the community district.
mih_option names the options mapped there (Option 1, 2, 3 and the Workforce Option, which ZR 27-131 calls Option 4).
instructions: Test the parcel's own point (PLUTO latitude and longitude), not a listing geocode.
Read the options mapped for the area, then apply ZR 27-131 for the set-aside, income bands and exemptions; outside every area, the UAP of ZR 27-111 may apply instead.
prerequisites: Parcel latitude and longitude, or a BBL to look them up in PLUTO.
restrictions: Public anonymous reads. The whole layer is about 300 KB, so a client may load it once and test points locally.
limitations: A zoning lot split by an area boundary needs the operative map; a lot point is one test.
Special purpose districts can impose MIH outside these polygons; check the special district text.
DCP updates the layer monthly; a recent rezoning may not appear yet.
verification: 2026-10-18: catalog HTTP 200, current version 20260331, 275 adopted areas with mih_option values.
2026-10-18: intersects query at the Caton Flats site returned that area with Option 2.

name: NYC zoning map layers (districts, commercial overlays, special districts)
publisher: NYC Department of City Planning
questions: Which zoning districts, overlays and special districts cover this lot today?
How much of a split lot lies in each district?
Has the lot been rezoned since the PLUTO release?
outline: nyzd has one polygon per mapped district with ZONEDIST (PARK marks mapped parkland); nyco has OVERLAY; nysp has SDNAME and SDLBL.
Polygons tile the city, so intersecting them with the MapPLUTO lot outline gives each district's share of the lot.

templates.purpose: Districts intersecting a lot's bounding box

instructions: Intersect the returned polygons with the lot outline; do not treat a bounding-box hit as coverage.
Ignore shares under about 1 percent: districts and tax lots are digitized separately, so lots show slivers of the districts across their lot lines.
For a split lot, sum each portion's area times its district's FAR (ZR 77-22) and apply use and bulk rules by portion, subject to ZR 77-11 and 77-02.
prerequisites: The lot's BBL for its MapPLUTO outline.
restrictions: Public anonymous reads; 2,000 features per query.
limitations: The layers show the map as DCP maintains it; an amendment adopted days ago may not be drawn yet.
A zoning lot can span several tax lots; the share is of the tax lot only.
verification: 2026-10-18: nyzd, nyco and nysp layers last edited 2026-09-30, newer than PLUTO 26v2 and the Open Data Zoning Tax Lot Database (last updated 2026-04-05).
2026-10-18: 237 17 Street, Brooklyn (PLUTO R6A/R6B split) returned R6A 54.7%, R6B 32.7%, PARK 12.6% and C2-4 overlay 62.6%.

name: Digital City Map street centerlines with mapped widths
publisher: NYC Department of City Planning
questions: Is the street this lot fronts a wide street (75 ft or more)?
Which mapped streets does the lot front, and how wide are they?
outline: One line per street segment with Street_NM, Streetwidth, Feat_Type (Mapped_St, Former_St, Not_mapped) and Feat_status.
Streetwidth is a number, an approximation (~60), a bound (<60, >100) or a range (60-100).
instructions: A street fronts the lot when its centerline lies within about half its width of the lot line.
A wide street is 75 ft or more (ZR 12-10); a bound or range settles it only when it is wholly on one side of 75 ft.
prerequisites: The lot outline from MapPLUTO.
restrictions: Public anonymous reads.
limitations: Widths are mapped widths, not built roadway widths; ZR 12-10 also treats some narrower streets as wide (for example along a park), which the map does not show.
verification: 2026-10-18: 120 Broadway returned Broadway 77 ft (wide), Nassau Street 49 ft, Pine Street 34.6-35.9 ft and Cedar Street 33-34.5 ft.
2026-10-18: 1176 Ocean Avenue, Brooklyn returned Ocean Avenue 100 ft as its front street.

name: Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) projects and their lots
publisher: NYC Department of City Planning / NYC Open Data
questions: Has City Planning acted on this lot (special permit, authorization, certification, rezoning)?
How did a nearby project get more floor area than the base district allows?
outline: 2iga-a6mk maps each project_id to the BBLs it covers.

hgx4-8ukb has one row per project: project_name, project_brief, public_status, actions (ZS special permit, ZA authorization, ZC certification, ZM map change, ZR text change and others), ulurp_numbers and milestone dates.
instructions: Look up project ids by BBL, then read the projects; area-wide rezonings list every lot they cover, so separate a lot-specific action from a neighborhood plan.
prerequisites: The lot's BBL; for a condominium, also its original lot.
restrictions: Public anonymous reads.
limitations: BSA variances and special permits are not in ZAP.
Older projects may lack BBL validation or full action lists.

templates.purpose: Monthly copy into the deal store
templates.endpointLabel: Counts CSV (one row per BBL, uc2018 to uc2024 with the statement of account PDF per year)

name: NYC Zoning Resolution
publisher: NYC Department of City Planning / City Planning Commission
questions: What use, floor area, height or setback rules apply in this zoning district?
What special district rules or development-right provisions apply?
outline: Articles I-VII contain general, use, bulk, parking and other district rules; II covers residence, III commercial, IV manufacturing.
Articles VIII-XIV contain special purpose district rules. Chapters and numbered sections provide precise citations.
Appendices, referenced maps and amendments may qualify an individual section.
instructions: Use acres_discover_tools to obtain current read-only search/content tools, then acres_execute_tool to retrieve relevant sections and referenced exceptions.
Start with the parcel's district and special district; follow the site's actual section links instead of guessing URL slugs.
Record section identifiers and the page's amendment information. Consult historical releases for an as-of question.
prerequisites: District, special district or precise zoning topic; often a confirmed parcel.
restrictions: Public pages; no supported general-purpose API was verified.
limitations: Homepage and release index verified, but an end-to-end section search/content tool run was not tested for this registry.
A successful page fetch does not establish applicability or legal effective date; referenced maps and approvals can change the result.
verification: 2026-10-11: homepage HTTP 200 and article organization read.
2026-10-11: dated downloads page read; no full PDF mirrored.

outline: 3h2n-5cm9 lists DOB violations by boro, zero-padded block and lot, issue_date (YYYYMMDD), violation_type, violation_category (an asterisk marks dismissed or resolved; ACTIVE is open), disposition_date and description.

name: NYC HPD Multiple Dwelling Registrations
publisher: NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development / NYC Open Data
questions: Is this building a registered multiple dwelling with HPD, and is the registration current?

outline: tesw-yqqr lists one row per registered building: registrationid, buildingid, boroid, bare block and lot, bin, address, lastregistrationdate and registrationenddate (the registration year ends on this date; an earlier date is a lapsed registration).
Owners of buildings with three or more residential units, and of one- or two-unit buildings not owner-occupied, must register annually.

templates.purpose: Read the lot's HPD registration status via specialist tool

instructions: Use acres_nyc_public_records with the 10-digit BBL and read hpdRegistration (status current, expired or none, last registration date, registration end date, buildings).
The deal store reads the same feed in batches for every matched lot; a current registration raises the tenant screen's confidence that a 3+ unit pre-1974 building is an occupied multiple dwelling.
prerequisites: 10-digit NYC BBL.
restrictions: Public NYC Open Data Socrata API; send the app token and respect rate limits.
limitations: Registration records occupancy class and owner contacts, not a rent-stabilized unit count or tenancy roster. A missing registration may mean a one- or two-family owner-occupied building, or non-compliance.

name: LoopNet NYC Sale Listings

accessPoints.label: LoopNet New York City commercial real estate for sale

outline: The five boroughs are searched as overlapping boxes, split in four whenever a box reaches LoopNet's 750-result cap, and paged; each listing is read once by its LoopNet ID.
Whole-lot sale listings only: multifamily, land, industrial and flex, retail, office and mixed use. Condo and co-op units, portfolios, hotels, special-purpose property and leases are skipped.
Listings are matched to their PLUTO lot by pin coordinates and address (GeoSearch confirms the house number) and priced per buildable square foot like every other deal.

restrictions: Facts and the listing link only: no descriptions, photos or agent contacts are stored (CoStar v. Crexi, 2025). Link to the LoopNet page for the offering itself.
limitations: LoopNet does not claim an exhaustive inventory and the search API depends on a renewed LoopNet session; a pass during an outage keeps the previous rows.

verification: 2026-10-18: live Brooklyn-box search through the LoopNet API (24 searches, 852 cards) ingested into a copy of the production deal store: 632 whole-lot listings, 533 matched to PLUTO lots, 406 with 500+ sq ft of unused floor area, 90 deferred to MLS or broker rows on the same lot.

outline: The public RSS feed is read on the deal store's scheduled market refresh, newest page first, with archive pages (?paged=N) walked once for the backfill. robots.txt is honored, requests identify as ArosaBot and wait two seconds apart.
Each story keeps only what the feed carries: headline, link, publish date and the feed's short summary.

Street addresses in the headline, summary and the feed's own tags are resolved with NYC Planning GeoSearch. Stories that name a building only by its name, or an address that exists in more than one borough with no borough in the same sentence, are not linked to a lot.
Roundups and profiles naming more than five addresses are not linked to any lot.

Stories that name a building only by its name, or an address that exists in more than one borough with no borough in the same sentence, are not linked to a lot.
Roundups and profiles naming more than five addresses are not linked to any lot.
verification: 2026-10-21: three pages of the live national feed (51 stories) parsed; 15 linked to NYC lots, including 2 Gansevoort Street and 511 Fifth Avenue. Out-of-city stories were not linked.
